title: Alimi Ballard Joins General Hospital Cast
seoTitle: Alimi Ballard Joins General Hospital Cast
subtitle: The actor takes on the role of William Baines in the television production
excerpt: Actor Alimi Ballard has been confirmed to join the cast of the television production General Hospital, marking his return to the world of daily soaps.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Actor Alimi Ballard has been confirmed as the newest member of the General Hospital cast, where he will portray the character William Baines. His debut on the production is scheduled for Thursday, September 3.

Return to Daily Soaps

With this casting, the actor returns to the television genre that marked the beginning of his artistic career. He got his first big acting break in 1993, when he played Frankie Hubbard in the production Loving, a character he continued to portray in The City starting in 1995.

Memories of Early Career

In a previous interview with Theatre Corner, the actor recalled the period when he played the son of the couple Angie and Jesse Hubbard, portrayed by Debbi Morgan and Darnell Williams. He highlighted Debbi Morgan's importance in his initial professional development, emphasizing what he learned about the level of intensity and dedication required in the profession.

Experience in Television and Film

After concluding his participation in the soap opera in 1996, the actor built an expressive career in primetime television. He was part of the cast of well-known productions, such as the role of Quizmaster in Sabrina the Teenage Witch and FBI agent David Sinclair in Numb3rs, in addition to appearances in Criminal Minds, Queen Sugar, Queen of the South, Law & Order, and The Rookie.

The Challenges of the Acting Profession

The artist also recalled periods of financial instability faced between the film Deep Impact and the start of filming for Numb3rs. He mentioned months dealing with financial uncertainties, periods of unemployment benefits, and the need for resilience in an artistic career.

With information from Yahoo.
